authority: California State Water Resources Control Board
locator: 2022 CGP FAQs: when coverage is required
evidence: a larger common plan of development or sale that in total disturbs one or more acres
summary: Clearing, excavation or other covered construction disturbing at least one acre needs CGP coverage; aggregate smaller phases within the same development. The Lake Tahoe Hydrologic Unit uses a separate Lahontan permit.

locator: GAR100001, Part I.A; stand-alone projects
evidence: stand alone construction projects that will result in land disturbance equal to or greater than one (1) acre
summary: GAR100001 covers qualifying construction stormwater discharges from stand-alone projects disturbing at least one acre. Do not use this stand-alone instrument to decide coverage for a multi-project common development.

locator: NPDES Permit for Construction Activities; Phase I and Phase II
evidence: Phase II reduces that project size to 1 acre or more
summary: Illinois EPA describes the construction stormwater permit threshold as one acre, including qualifying disturbance aggregated across a larger development. The five-acre threshold discussed in the preceding sentence is the older Phase I threshold.

locator: Construction Activity: CGP applicability, Section 8.3
evidence: Discharge stormwater to surface waters of the state or to a municipal separate storm sewer system
summary: Apply Florida's construction CGP test to both disturbance and drainage: at least one acre or a smaller portion of a common development, and runoff discharging to state surface waters or a municipal storm sewer.

authority: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation
locator: Construction Activity Permit: introductory applicability and NYC watershed exceptions
evidence: activities that will disturb 5,000 square feet or more, but less than one acre
summary: The general construction threshold is one acre; an individual SPDES permit is an alternative. DEC also specifies 5,000 square feet in the NYC East of Hudson watershed and 20,000 square feet in NYC municipal boundaries, with smaller NYC components of a qualifying common development included. Within NYC creating at least 5,000 square feet of impervious area is also covered.

locator: Construction Stormwater General Permit: sites required to apply
evidence: Sites that disturb one acre or more
summary: For projects with stormwater discharge to surface waters, screen one acre of disturbed land and the combined disturbance of a larger development. Ecology can designate smaller sites that significantly contribute pollutants.

authority: New Jersey Department of Agriculture / Soil Conservation Program
locator: NJDEP's Stormwater Discharger Permit: permit 5G3
evidence: in addition to a Soil Erosion and Sediment Control Plan certification
summary: New Jersey directs construction disturbing at least one acre to obtain 5G3 authorization in addition to soil erosion and sediment control plan certification from the local Soil Conservation District.

locator: Water Quality Permits FAQ: Is a DEQ permit required for construction activities?
evidence: Projects that disturb one acre or more over a period of time or are part of a common plan
summary: Oregon identifies 1200-C coverage for qualifying construction activity disturbing an acre or more, including cumulative disturbance over time or under a common plan. Submit an erosion and sediment control plan for approval before starting.

authority: North Carolina Department of Environmental Quality
locator: NPDES Construction Program: NCG01 and NCG25 permits
evidence: part of a larger common plan of development of that size
summary: The program applies at one acre of disturbance, including smaller components of a qualifying plan. NCG01 applies to sites subject to the DEMLR Sediment Program; NCG25 addresses other construction subject to the Clean Water Act.

locator: Construction Stormwater: activities requiring permits
evidence: Construction activities with earth disturbances greater than or equal to one acre
summary: Pennsylvania requires NPDES coverage for qualifying construction disturbing at least one acre. The listed category excludes agricultural plowing or tilling, animal heavy use areas, timber harvesting and road maintenance; these exclusions do not describe a data-center pad.

authority: Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy
locator: Construction Stormwater overview: permit by rule
evidence: the applicant/permittee receives automatic stormwater coverage upon the applicant obtaining a Part 91 permit
summary: One or more disturbed acres with a point-source stormwater discharge to state waters falls under the state construction program. For eligible smaller sites, Part 91 authorization can provide automatic coverage; at five acres or more EGLE requires a notice of coverage application to the Water Resources Division.

locator: Applicability of the CSGP: Construction Activity
evidence: Areas smaller than one (1) acre are also regulated under the CSGP
summary: Indiana's CSGP applies at one acre of land disturbance; a smaller project is regulated when it is within a qualifying larger common plan of development or sale.

authority: Utah Department of Environmental Quality, Division of Water Quality
locator: UPDES Permits: Storm Water; What type of permit do I need?
evidence: This permit also covers non-residential disturbances less than an acre that are part of a common plan
summary: Nonresidential construction uses Utah's general construction permit at one acre or more, including qualifying sub-acre disturbances within a common plan. The separately named Common Plan Permit on this page is for certain single residential lots.

authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes / Pollution Control Agency
locator: Minnesota Rules, chapter 7090: construction activity definition
evidence: land disturbance of equal to or greater than one acre
summary: Minnesota's construction activity definition includes clearing, grading and excavation that disturbs at least one acre, and smaller disturbance within a development or sale plan that in total reaches one acre.

locator: Construction Sites – One Acre or More: who needs a permit and approval process
evidence: could impact a receiving water or its tributaries within a quarter mile of the site
summary: Nevada screens at one disturbed acre, including qualifying common plans. The Stormwater Branch may also require coverage below one acre when it determines a nearby receiving water or tributary could be affected; an approval letter is required before construction.

locator: Construction site storm water permit overview; Wis. Admin. Code NR 216 subch. III
evidence: where one or more acres of land will be disturbed must submit an application
summary: Landowners of most projects disturbing one acre or more must send a notice of intent to request coverage. Phased disturbance in common developments can count even if work occurs on different schedules.

authority: Kentucky Energy and Environment Cabinet, Division of Water
locator: Stormwater General Construction Permit fact sheet; applicability
evidence: The permit is also required for smaller sites that are part of a larger, common plan of development
summary: Kentucky's construction stormwater program applies to clearing, grading or excavation disturbing one acre or more, and to smaller components of a qualifying common development. Operators must plan for and implement stormwater controls.

authority: Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation
locator: NPDES Stormwater Construction Permit: who needs coverage
evidence: less than one acre if it is part of a larger common plan of development or sale
summary: Tennessee covers construction sites where clearing, grading or excavation disturbs at least one acre, or less when part of a qualifying common plan.

authority: South Carolina Department of Environmental Services
locator: Stormwater Construction Activities: which construction sites are regulated?
evidence: within ½ mile of a receiving water body in South Carolina’s Coastal Zone
summary: South Carolina lists one acre, smaller phases in a common development, and a distinct Coastal Zone screen for construction within half a mile of a receiving water. Check the coastal program before using acreage alone.

locator: Do I need permit coverage? Site criteria and Lake Martin special designation
evidence: A site that will disturb one or more acres of land
summary: One disturbed acre or a qualifying common plan totaling one acre triggers construction coverage. At Lake Martin, nonexempt disturbance below one acre also requires coverage under the special designation.

authority: Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
locator: Construction Stormwater GP: applicability table, locally approvable construction
evidence: Local approval satisfies state permit requirements
summary: For locally approvable private projects from one to under five acres, the state table specifies local approval and an erosion and sediment control plan without separate state registration. The locally approvable private category at five or more acres also requires registration.

locator: 20-CP General Permit FAQ: General Background
evidence: Operators must have coverage under the State’s General Permit
summary: Maryland's 20-CP covers qualifying construction disturbing at least one acre and smaller disturbances in a common development that will ultimately disturb that much land.

locator: Construction or Land Disturbance: land disturbance permits
evidence: one or more acres over the life of the project
summary: Missouri requires land disturbance permits for construction disturbing at least one acre. Smaller phases count when their common development or sale plan cumulatively reaches one acre over its life.

locator: OKR10 Construction Stormwater: who needs a permit?
evidence: Less than one acre if that activity is part of a “larger common plan of development or sale”
summary: Oklahoma directs owners or operators disturbing one acre or more to OKR10. It describes smaller activities within a common plan that exceeds one acre as covered as well.

locator: Construction General Permits FAQ: LAR100000 and LAR200000
evidence: LDEQ requires the submission of a Notice of Intent
summary: Louisiana differentiates small construction (one to under five acres) from large construction (five or more acres). A notice of intent is required for the large category, including phases of a common plan whose cumulative disturbance reaches five acres.

locator: Construction Stormwater: large and small general permits
evidence: Small Construction (1 to less than 5 acres)
summary: Mississippi lists distinct general permits for small construction (one to under five acres) and large construction (five or more). MDEQ states the small permit was administratively continued pending reissuance.

locator: NER210000: regulated small and large construction activity
evidence: land disturbance of equal to or greater than one acre
summary: Nebraska's NER210000 applies at one disturbed acre and to smaller construction within a qualifying common plan. The archived permit states an expiration of November 30, 2026; check its successor for later work.

locator: ARR150000, cover and Parts I.B.6 and definitions
evidence: Small construction sites eligible for coverage under this CGP will be considered to have automatic coverage
summary: Arkansas's permit effective November 1, 2026 includes qualifying construction disturbing at least one acre in total, including smaller component areas. Eligible small sites receive automatic coverage subject to the conditions in Part I.B.6.

locator: IPDES Permits: Stormwater — Construction General Permit (CGP)
evidence: Construction projects that disturb one or more acres and discharge stormwater must be permitted
summary: Idaho DEQ requires construction CGP coverage where at least one acre is disturbed and stormwater discharges, including qualifying smaller common-plan sites. DEQ describes a low-erosivity waiver for eligible projects under five acres.

locator: Maine Revised Statutes, Title 38 §420-D: opening prohibition and scope
evidence: one acre or more of disturbed area without prior approval from the department
summary: Maine's state stormwater law requires prior department approval for covered projects disturbing at least one acre in organized areas. This is the state statutory project-approval trigger; it does not establish eligibility for a separate discharge permit.

authority: Delaware Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Control
locator: Sediment and Stormwater: construction general permit
evidence: 1 acre or more must submit a Notice of Intent (NOI) prior to plan approval
summary: Delaware directs construction with at least one acre of land disturbance to submit a notice of intent before plan approval and comply with the Delaware CGP.

locator: Construction Stormwater Discharge Permits: when coverage is required
evidence: total earth disturbance of equal or greater than one (1) acre of land area
summary: Vermont requires coverage for construction disturbing at least one acre and for smaller portions of a larger common plan that reaches the threshold. Review the permit's stabilization and concurrent-disturbance requirements as well.

authority: Rhode Island Secretary of State / Department of Environmental Management
locator: 250-RICR-150-10-1 §1.4(A)(112): small construction activity
evidence: land disturbance of equal to or greater than one acre and less than five acres
summary: Rhode Island defines small construction stormwater discharges to include clearing, grading or excavation disturbing one to under five acres, including smaller disturbances within a qualifying larger plan. The definition concerns discharges, not zoning approval.

authority: Hawaii Department of Health, Clean Water Branch
locator: Construction General Permit FAQ, questions 1–3
evidence: Any activity that disturbs one (1) acre or more of land
summary: Hawaii's Clean Water Branch directs applicants to construction stormwater coverage when one acre is disturbed or a smaller site belongs to a development that cumulatively disturbs at least one acre.

locator: Final AKR100000 fact sheet; covered construction and discharge receptors
evidence: where those discharges enter waters of the U.S.
summary: Alaska's 2026 general permit covers qualifying construction disturbing at least one acre when discharges enter U.S. waters directly or through a conveyance or enter a municipal separate storm sewer. Check EPA-retained areas separately.

authority: North Dakota Department of Environmental Quality
locator: General Construction Stormwater Permit FAQ, question 1
evidence: equal to or greater than one (1) acre
summary: North Dakota's program FAQ sets a one-acre disturbance threshold including sub-acre portions of a development whose combined disturbance reaches one acre.

authority: South Dakota Department of Agriculture and Natural Resources
locator: Stormwater Permit for Construction Activities: covered activity
evidence: Construction activities disturbing one or more acres must have coverage
summary: South Dakota includes one-acre construction, qualifying larger common plans, phased construction and related support activities in its construction stormwater permitting screen.

locator: Large and Small Construction General Permit: LCGP and SCGP
evidence: at least one acre, but less than five acres
summary: Wyoming lists separate small (one to under five acres) and large (at least five acres) construction stormwater permits. A smaller disturbance can fall into either category based on the ultimate common-plan size.

locator: MPDES, Stormwater Construction (SWC) — MTR100000
evidence: Authorization under the SWC is required for construction activities that disturb one or more acres of land
summary: Montana requires SWC authorization for qualifying construction disturbing at least one acre. Its program includes excavation, grading, grubbing and placing or removing earth in the disturbance screen.

authority: West Virginia Department of Environmental Protection
locator: Construction Stormwater General Permit: program overview
evidence: including smaller sites that are part of a larger common plan of development
summary: West Virginia requires operators disturbing at least one acre, or smaller sites in a qualifying common plan, to obtain authorization for construction stormwater discharge under its WV/NPDES program.

authority: Colorado General Assembly, Office of Legislative Legal Services
locator: 2026 Colorado Revised Statutes, §25-8-501(1): permits required for discharge of pollutants
evidence: from a point source without first having obtained a permit from the division
summary: Colorado requires a division permit before discharging a pollutant from a point source to state water and prohibits routing it through a ditch or man-made conveyance to avoid the requirement. This is the general statutory discharge trigger; it does not establish the construction CGP acreage, exemptions or eligibility.

authority: Kansas Legislature / Kansas Secretary of State
locator: 2025 Kansas Session Laws, ch. 67 §4; K.S.A. 75-5676
evidence: the secretary of health and environment shall issue an authorization, waiver or denial
summary: After submission of a complete construction stormwater notice of intent or rainfall erosivity waiver application with supporting documents, Kansas gives the secretary 45 days to authorize, waive or deny, subject to conflicting federal law. This state decision deadline is not automatic authorization or an acreage threshold.

authority: US Virgin Islands Department of Planning and Natural Resources
locator: Directions for applying for the territorial construction general permit, page 1
evidence: Professional Engineer licensed in the VI, and then stamped by a Professional Engineer
summary: For a project covered by the territorial construction general permit, DPNR's posted application directions require a notice of intent, fees and a stormwater pollution prevention plan developed or reviewed and stamped by a VI-licensed professional engineer. The precise acreage boundary is not resolved by these directions.
